# Open Lakehouse

> The Open Lakehouse: open source data engineering and the agentic lakehouse, with Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, MLflow and Apache Spark. Your data in open formats on storage you control, ready for AI agents.

This file follows the llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org). It lists
the canonical pages on this site that are safe and useful to cite. The
full text of every article is mirrored in /llms-full.txt.

## Site
- [Home](https://openlakehouse.io/): What the Open Lakehouse is and why it matters.
- [Technologies](https://openlakehouse.io/technologies): Every open-source building block, grouped by layer.
- [Open Source Data Engineering](https://openlakehouse.io/open-source-data-engineering): What open source data engineering is, the reference stack, and the projects that make it up.
- [Agentic Lakehouse](https://openlakehouse.io/agentic-lakehouse): What an agentic lakehouse is: open tables, a catalog agents can read, MCP tools, declarative pipelines, policies and tracing.
- [Agentic Data Engineering](https://openlakehouse.io/agentic-data-engineering): How AI agents write, test and run data pipelines while the platform enforces scope, dry runs and policies.
- [Spark Masterclass](https://openlakehouse.io/spark-masterclass): Spark Masterclass is a free, open-source online book on Apache Spark 4.3: 92 chapters from execution fundamentals to SQL, Spark Connect, streaming, Declarative Pipelines and internals, each backed by runnable code and saved output.
- [Spark Matrix](https://openlakehouse.io/spark-matrix): Spark Matrix compares Apache Spark features across managed Spark platforms such as Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, Databricks, Google Cloud, Microsoft Fabric and Snowflake. Every cell is traced to the Apache Spark source or a primary vendor statement.
- [Reference Architectures](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures): Interactive open source data engineering reference architectures, each backed by a runnable repo, with industry lenses.
- [Learn](https://openlakehouse.io/learn): Curated guides, talks, and tutorials.
- [Community](https://openlakehouse.io/community): Where practitioners gather.
- [Authors](https://openlakehouse.io/authors): Maintainers, authors, and practitioners in the Open Lakehouse community.
- [Blog](https://openlakehouse.io/blog): Release notes, deep dives, and republished posts from upstream projects.
- [FAQ](https://openlakehouse.io/faq): Direct, citable Q&A about the Open Lakehouse, Delta Lake, Iceberg, Unity Catalog, MLflow, and Spark.
- [Podcast](https://openlakehouse.io/podcast): This Week in Open Lakehouse: a weekly podcast on open source data engineering news, with show notes and transcripts.

Every cell is traced to the Apache Spark source or a primary vendor statement. Data build 2026-11-23. Cite this page.

## Open Data Engineering Reference
- [Open Data Engineering Reference](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Main_Page): Cited, versioned answers for building data platforms you control. A free, open reference for open source data engineering: table formats, catalogs, engines, pipelines, and the AI agents that work on them. Every fact is cited, dated, and tied to a version. Each article is also served as Markdown at its URL plus .md.
- [Accumulator](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Accumulator): In Apache Spark, an accumulator is a shared variable that tasks can only add to, through an associative and commutative operation, and whose total only the driver can read.
- [Adaptive Query Execution](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Adaptive_Query_Execution): Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) is the part of Spark SQL in Apache Spark that re-optimizes a query while it runs, using statistics measured on completed shuffle stages instead of estimates made before the query started.
- [Agentic lakehouse](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Agentic_lakehouse): An agentic lakehouse is an open lakehouse built so that AI agents can find, query and change data under controls that the platform enforces.
- [Aggregate pushdown](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Aggregate_pushdown): Aggregate pushdown is a query optimization in which an engine hands an aggregate such as COUNT(*), MIN(col) or MAX(col) to the data source, which answers it from metadata or computes it itself, instead of returning every row for the engine to aggregate.
- [Apache Airflow](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Airflow): Apache Airflow is an open source platform for developing, scheduling and monitoring workflows, such as batch data pipelines and machine learning jobs, in which each workflow is defined as Python code.
- [Apache Celeborn](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Celeborn): Apache Celeborn is an open source remote shuffle service: a cluster of master and worker servers that stores and serves the intermediate shuffle data of Apache Spark, Apache Flink and Hadoop MapReduce jobs, so that the data does not live on the compute nodes' local disks.
- [Apache DataFusion Comet](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_DataFusion_Comet): Apache DataFusion Comet (usually just Comet) is an open source plugin for Apache Spark that replaces supported Spark SQL operators and expressions with implementations that process Apache Arrow columnar data, most of them native Rust code built on the Apache DataFusion query engine.
- [Apache Gluten](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Gluten): Apache Gluten is an open source plugin for Apache Spark that converts Spark SQL physical plans into plans for a native engine, such as Velox or ClickHouse, and runs the supported parts of a query in native code instead of in the Java virtual machine (JVM).
- [Apache Hive](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Hive): Apache Hive is a distributed SQL data warehouse system that runs queries over files in distributed storage, together with the Hive Metastore, a service that stores table metadata for Hive and for other engines.
- [Apache Hudi](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Hudi): Apache Hudi (pronounced "hoodie") is an open table format and data lake platform that adds tables, transactions, record-level upserts and deletes, indexes and table services to data stored in open file formats on a data lake.
- [Apache Iceberg](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Iceberg): Apache Iceberg is an open table format for large analytic tables stored as files in a distributed file system or object store.
- [Apache Mesos support in Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Mesos_support_in_Spark): Apache Mesos support in Spark was the integration that let Apache Spark use Apache Mesos as its cluster manager: a Spark application pointed at a mesos:// master URL received resources from Mesos and ran its executors as Mesos tasks.
- [Apache Parquet](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Parquet): Apache Parquet is an open source, column-oriented data file format for efficient storage and retrieval of analytic data.
- [Apache Polaris](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Polaris): Apache Polaris is an open source catalog for Apache Iceberg tables that implements the Iceberg REST catalog API, so that several query engines can read and write the same tables through one catalog.
- [Apache Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Spark): Apache Spark is an open source, distributed engine for large-scale data processing, with high-level APIs in Java, Scala, Python and R and an optimized engine that runs general execution graphs.
- [Apache Uniffle](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Apache_Uniffle): Apache Uniffle is an open source remote shuffle service for distributed computing engines: a cluster of coordinators and shuffle servers that receives the shuffle data of Apache Spark, Hadoop MapReduce and Apache Tez jobs, stores it in memory, on local disk or in remote storage such as HDFS, and serves it to the tasks that read it.
- [Arrow-optimized Python UDF](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Arrow-optimized_Python_UDF): In PySpark, an Arrow-optimized Python UDF is a regular row-at-a-time Python user-defined function) whose input and output move between the JVM and the Python worker as Apache Arrow batches instead of pickled Python objects.
- [Bloom filter (data files)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Bloom_filter_(data_files)): A bloom filter in a data file is a compact, per-column structure that a writer stores inside a columnar file, such as an Apache Parquet or ORC file, so that a reader can tell that a value is definitely not in a row group without reading its data.
- [Broadcast join](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Broadcast_join): A broadcast join is a join strategy in which the smaller table is copied in full to every executor, so that each task can join its part of the larger table locally, without a shuffle of the larger table.
- [Broadcast variable](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Broadcast_variable): In Apache Spark, a broadcast variable is a read-only value that the driver sends once to every executor, where it is cached and shared by all tasks, instead of being shipped again with every task.
- [Bucketing](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Bucketing): Bucketing is a table layout in which rows are assigned to a fixed number of logical buckets by hashing the values of one or more bucket columns, so that all rows with the same key land in the same bucket; each bucket is stored as one or more files, whose names carry the bucket ID.
- [Business Source License](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Business_Source_License): The Business Source License (BSL, also written BUSL) is a source-available software license, published by MariaDB, under which the source code can be read, changed and redistributed, but production use is allowed only as far as the licensor's Additional Use Grant permits, until each version converts to an open source license on its Change Date.
- [Caching and persistence](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Caching_and_persistence): In Apache Spark, caching or persistence keeps the computed partitions of a DataFrame, table or RDD in executor memory or on local disk, so that later actions reuse them instead of recomputing them from the source.
- [Catalog plugin API (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Catalog_plugin_API_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, the catalog plugin API is the part of Data Source V2 that lets an external catalog register under a name and serve namespaces, tables, views, functions and procedures to Spark SQL; its root interface is org.apache.spark.sql.connector.catalog.CatalogPlugin.
- [Catalyst optimizer](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Catalyst_optimizer): The Catalyst optimizer is the extensible query optimizer of Spark SQL in Apache Spark; it turns every SQL query and DataFrame or Dataset program into an optimized physical plan by applying rules to trees in four phases: analysis, logical optimization, physical planning and code generation.
- [Checkpointing (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Checkpointing_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, checkpointing is saving data or query progress to storage so that later work can start from the saved copy instead of recomputing it, and the word names two different features.
- [Collation (Spark SQL)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Collation_(Spark_SQL)): In Apache Spark, a collation is a property of the STRING type that sets how Spark SQL compares, sorts, groups and joins string values, for example whether 'a' equals 'A'.
- [Column pruning](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Column_pruning): Column pruning is a query optimization in which an engine reads only the columns that a query uses, and drops every other column as early as possible in the plan, ideally before the data leaves storage.
- [Copy-on-write and merge-on-read](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Copy-on-write_and_merge-on-read): Copy-on-write and merge-on-read are the two strategies an open table format can use to apply row-level updates and deletes to data stored in immutable files.
- [Cost-based optimizer (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Cost-based_optimizer_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, the cost-based optimizer (CBO) is the part of the Catalyst optimizer that uses table and column statistics, such as row counts, distinct values and minimum and maximum values, to estimate how many rows each step of a query produces, and uses those estimates to choose join orders and join strategies.
- [Data catalog](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Data_catalog): A data catalog, in a lakehouse, is the service that names tables and other data assets, records where each table's current metadata lives, coordinates commits, and decides who may read or write each asset.
- [Data skew](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Data_skew): Data skew is an uneven distribution of data across the partitions of a distributed computation, so that a few tasks process far more data than the rest and the whole stage waits for them.
- [Data Source V2](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Data_Source_V2): Data Source V2 (DSV2) is the connector API of Apache Spark: a set of Java interfaces in the org.apache.spark.sql.connector package that lets an external system plug its catalogs, tables, reads and writes into Spark's query planning and execution.
- [DataFrame](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/DataFrame): A DataFrame is a table-like data structure made of named columns, each with a data type, and rows.
- [Dataset (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Dataset_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, a Dataset is a strongly typed, distributed collection of objects of one JVM type T that can be transformed in parallel with functional operations such as map and filter or with relational operations such as select and groupBy.
- [Deletion vector](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Deletion_vector): A deletion vector (DV) is a compact bitmap, stored outside a data file, that marks which rows of that data file are deleted.
- [Delta Lake](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Delta_Lake): Delta Lake is an open table format and storage framework that adds ACID transactions to tables stored as Apache Parquet files in a distributed file system or object store.
- [Directed acyclic graph (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, the directed acyclic graph (DAG) of a job is the graph of datasets and the operations that connect them; Spark's DAG scheduler cuts this graph into stages at shuffle boundaries and runs the stages in dependency order.
- [Driver (Apache Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Driver_(Apache_Spark)): In Apache Spark, the driver is the process that runs an application's main() function, creates the SparkContext, turns the program into tasks and schedules those tasks on executors.
- [DuckDB](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/DuckDB): DuckDB is an open source, in-process SQL database management system designed for analytical query workloads.
- [Dynamic allocation](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Dynamic_allocation): Dynamic allocation is an Apache Spark feature that adds executors to an application when tasks are waiting and removes executors that sit idle, so that an application holds only the resources its current work needs.
- [Dynamic partition pruning](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Dynamic_partition_pruning): Dynamic partition pruning (DPP) is a query optimization in Apache Spark that skips partitions of a table using filter values that are only known while the query runs, typically the join keys that survive a filter on the other side of a join.
- [Encoder (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Encoder_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, an encoder is the object that converts a JVM object of type T to and from Spark SQL's internal row representation; every typed Dataset) needs one for its element type.
- [Event time and processing time](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Event_time_and_processing_time): In stream processing, event time is the time at which an event actually happened, recorded in the event itself, and processing time is the time on the clock of the machine that handles the event.
- [Exactly-once semantics](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Exactly-once_semantics): In stream processing, exactly-once semantics is the guarantee that each input record affects the result exactly once, with nothing lost and nothing duplicated, even when parts of the system fail and work is retried.
- [Executor](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Executor): In Apache Spark, an executor is a process launched for one application on a worker node; it runs the application's tasks and keeps data in memory or on disk between them.
- [Executor decommissioning](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Executor_decommissioning): In Apache Spark, executor decommissioning is the graceful shutdown of an executor: Spark stops sending it new tasks and, when storage decommissioning is on, copies its cached RDD blocks and shuffle files to other executors or to fallback storage before the executor exits.
- [Executor memory overhead](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Executor_memory_overhead): In Apache Spark, executor memory overhead is the memory that Spark requests for each executor container on top of the JVM heap, to cover everything in the container that is not on the heap: JVM internals, native libraries, Python worker processes and other processes.
- [External shuffle service](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/External_shuffle_service): In Apache Spark, the external shuffle service (ESS) is a long-running process on each node of a cluster that serves the shuffle files written by executors, so those files stay available after the executor that wrote them has been removed or has failed.
- [foreachBatch](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/ForeachBatch): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, foreachBatch is a sink that calls a user function once for every micro-batch, passing the batch's output as an ordinary DataFrame together with a unique batch id, so that any batch API can be used to write it.
- [Garbage collection in Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Garbage_collection_in_Spark): Garbage collection in Spark is the work the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) does inside each Apache Spark executor and driver to find objects that are no longer used and free their memory.
- [GPU acceleration in Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/GPU_acceleration_in_Spark): GPU acceleration in Spark is the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to run parts of an Apache Spark application, either by scheduling GPUs to tasks that use them directly (for example deep learning training) or by replacing Spark SQL operators with GPU implementations.
- [GraphFrames](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/GraphFrames): GraphFrames is an open source graph processing package for Apache Spark that represents a graph as a pair of Spark DataFrames, one of vertices and one of edges, and provides graph algorithms, the Pregel and AggregateMessages APIs, and a motif-finding query language on top of them.
- [GraphX](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/GraphX): GraphX is the graph processing library of Apache Spark: it extends Spark's resilient distributed dataset (RDD) with a property graph, a directed multigraph with user-defined properties on each vertex and edge, and provides graph operators, a Pregel API and a library of graph algorithms.
- [Higher-order functions (Spark SQL)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Higher-order_functions_(Spark_SQL)): In Apache Spark SQL, a higher-order function is a built-in function that takes a lambda function as an argument and applies it to the elements of an array or the entries of a map, such as transform, filter and aggregate.
- [Hive Metastore](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Hive_Metastore): The Hive Metastore (HMS) is the metadata service of Apache Hive: it stores the names, schemas, partitions and storage locations of tables in a relational database and serves them to engines through a Thrift API.
- [Hive on Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Hive_on_Spark): Hive on Spark was an execution engine option in Apache Hive that ran HiveQL queries as Apache Spark jobs instead of MapReduce or Apache Tez jobs; users turned it on with set hive.execution.engine=spark;.
- [Iceberg File Format API](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Iceberg_File_Format_API): The Iceberg File Format API is a set of Java interfaces in Apache Iceberg that puts every data file format behind one common reader and writer contract, so that engines read and write Iceberg data files through a registry instead of format-specific code.
- [Iceberg position delete](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Iceberg_position_delete): In Apache Iceberg, a position delete marks one row as deleted by naming the data file that holds it and the row's position in that file, counting from zero.
- [Iceberg REST catalog](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Iceberg_REST_catalog): The Iceberg REST catalog is an OpenAPI specification, maintained in the Apache Iceberg project, that defines an HTTP interface between Iceberg clients and a catalog service.
- [INT96 timestamp](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/INT96_timestamp): An INT96 timestamp is a timestamp stored in the 12-byte INT96 physical type of Apache Parquet: 8 bytes of nanoseconds within the day followed by 4 bytes of day number.
- [Job, stage and task](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Job,_stage_and_task): In Apache Spark, a job is the parallel computation that one action (such as collect or save) starts; Spark divides each job into stages at shuffle boundaries, and each stage into tasks, one per partition, which run on executors.
- [Join strategy hints](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Join_strategy_hints): In Apache Spark SQL, join strategy hints are comments of the form /+ HINT(table) /, or DataFrame.hint() calls, that ask the planner to use a specific physical join algorithm for a relation instead of the one it would pick from statistics.
- [Kubernetes Operator for Apache Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Kubernetes_Operator_for_Apache_Spark): The Kubernetes Operator for Apache Spark is software that runs Spark workloads on Kubernetes through the operator pattern: users describe a Spark application or cluster as a Kubernetes custom resource, and a controller creates and watches the driver, executor and other pods until the workload ends.
- [Lateral column alias](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Lateral_column_alias): A lateral column alias is a column alias defined in a SELECT list that later expressions in the same SELECT list can refer to, as in SELECT price qty AS total, total 0.2 AS tax; Apache Spark supports it since version 3.4.0.
- [Lazy evaluation](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Lazy_evaluation): In Apache Spark, lazy evaluation means that transformations such as filter, select or map do not compute anything when they are called; Spark only records them in a plan, and runs the plan when an action such as collect, count or a write needs a result.
- [Logical plan and physical plan](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Logical_plan_and_physical_plan): In Apache Spark, a logical plan is a tree that describes what a query computes (which tables, filters, joins and aggregates) without saying how, and a physical plan is the tree of executable operators, such as SortMergeJoin or HashAggregate, that Spark actually runs on the cluster.
- [Logical type](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Logical_type): A logical type is an annotation that tells a reader how to interpret a stored value, layered on top of a small set of physical (storage) types.
- [mapGroupsWithState and flatMapGroupsWithState](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/MapGroupsWithState_and_flatMapGroupsWithState): In Structured Streaming, mapGroupsWithState and flatMapGroupsWithState are the original operators for arbitrary stateful processing: they call a user function for each grouping key with that key's new values and a GroupState object that holds the key's state between micro-batches.
- [Matei Zaharia](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Matei_Zaharia): Matei Zaharia is a computer scientist known for starting Apache Spark, an open source engine for large-scale data processing.
- [Medallion architecture](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Medallion_architecture): A medallion architecture is a data design pattern that organizes the tables of a lakehouse into layers of increasing quality, usually called bronze, silver and gold.
- [MinIO](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/MinIO): MinIO is an object storage server, written in Go, that implements the Amazon S3 API, so that tools written for S3 can store and read objects on hardware or clusters that the operator runs.
- [MLlib](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/MLlib): MLlib is the machine learning library of Apache Spark.
- [Model Context Protocol](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Model_Context_Protocol): The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that connects applications built on large language models (LLMs) to external data sources and tools.
- [Narrow and wide transformations](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Narrow_and_wide_transformations): In Apache Spark, a narrow transformation is one where each output partition depends on a single input partition, so it runs inside the same task as the step before it; a wide transformation needs data from many input partitions and therefore causes a shuffle and a new stage.
- [Native execution engine (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Native_execution_engine_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, a native execution engine is a component that runs the physical operators of a Spark SQL or DataFrame query as vectorized, columnar code compiled to machine code (usually C++ or Rust) instead of as Java bytecode generated by Spark's whole-stage code generation in the Java virtual machine (JVM).
- [Open lakehouse](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Open_lakehouse): An open lakehouse is a data platform architecture in which tables are stored as open file formats on low-cost object storage, managed by an open table format, registered in an open data catalog, and processed by any compatible engine.
- [Open table format](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Open_table_format): An open table format is a publicly specified way of organizing data files and metadata on file or object storage so that a collection of files behaves as a single database table, with atomic commits, consistent snapshots and schema management.
- [Output mode](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Output_mode): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, the output mode of a streaming query says which rows of the query's result table are written to the sink after each trigger: only new rows (append), only rows that changed (update) or the whole result (complete).
- [Pandas API on Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Pandas_API_on_Spark): Pandas API on Spark (the pyspark.pandas module, also called pandas-on-Spark) is the part of PySpark in Apache Spark that implements the pandas DataFrame, Series and Index API on top of Spark, so code written for pandas can run distributed on a Spark cluster.
- [Pandas UDF](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Pandas_UDF): In Apache Spark, a pandas UDF (also called a vectorized UDF) is a Python user-defined function) that Spark runs on batches of rows: Spark sends each batch to a Python worker as Apache Arrow data, the function receives and returns pandas Series or DataFrame objects, and the results are sent back to the JVM.
- [Parameterized queries (Spark SQL)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Parameterized_queries_(Spark_SQL)): In Apache Spark SQL, a parameterized query is a SQL statement that contains typed placeholders, called parameter markers, whose values are supplied separately by the calling API instead of being written into the SQL text.
- [Partition](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Partition): A partition is a subset of a dataset that a system stores or processes as one unit.
- [Partition pruning](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Partition_pruning): Partition pruning is a query optimization in which an engine uses the filters of a query to skip whole partitions of a table, so that the files in partitions that cannot match are never listed or read.
- [Predicate pushdown](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Predicate_pushdown): Predicate pushdown is a query optimization in which an engine sends the filter conditions of a query (the predicates in a WHERE clause) down to the layer that reads the data, so that rows, files or whole partitions that cannot match are never read.
- [Project Nessie](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Project_Nessie): Project Nessie is an open source transactional data catalog for data lakes that versions table metadata with Git-like commits, branches and tags.
- [Project Tungsten](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Project_Tungsten): Project Tungsten is the name of an Apache Spark engineering initiative, started in 2015, to make Spark's execution more efficient in CPU and memory by managing memory explicitly, storing rows in a compact binary format, using CPU caches better and generating code at run time.
- [Push-based shuffle](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Push-based_shuffle): Push-based shuffle is an Apache Spark shuffle mode in which map tasks push their shuffle blocks to remote external shuffle services, which merge the blocks for each shuffle partition, so that reduce tasks can read a few large merged files instead of many small blocks.
- [pyspark-client](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Pyspark-client): pyspark-client is the pure-Python Spark Connect client for Apache Spark, published on PyPI, which lets a Python program use the PySpark DataFrame, SQL and streaming APIs against a remote Spark Connect server without a Java runtime or Spark JAR files on the client machine.
- [Python data source API (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Python_data_source_API_(Spark)): The Python data source API of Apache Spark is a set of PySpark base classes, in the module pyspark.sql.datasource, for writing a custom data source or sink entirely in Python and using it with spark.read, df.write, spark.readStream and writeStream.
- [Python UDTF](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Python_UDTF): In Apache Spark, a Python UDTF (Python user-defined table function) is a Python class, registered with PySpark, whose eval method can return zero or more rows for each call, so that the function produces a whole table instead of a single value.
- [RDD](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/RDD): In Apache Spark, a resilient distributed dataset (RDD) is an immutable collection of elements split into partitions across the nodes of a cluster, which can be processed in parallel and is rebuilt from its lineage when a partition is lost.
- [Real-time mode (Structured Streaming)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Real-time_mode_(Structured_Streaming)): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, real-time mode (Real-time Mode, RTM) is a streaming execution mode that runs long-lived tasks which process and emit each record as it arrives, instead of running a new short job for every micro-batch, to reach millisecond-scale end-to-end latency with the same DataFrame APIs and exactly-once processing guarantees.
- [Remote shuffle service](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Remote_shuffle_service): A remote shuffle service (RSS) is a cluster of long-running servers that receives, stores and serves the intermediate shuffle data of distributed jobs, so that the data no longer lives on the local disks of the compute processes that wrote it.
- [RocksDB state store](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/RocksDB_state_store): The RocksDB state store is a state store implementation for Apache Spark Structured Streaming that keeps the state of stateful operators in RocksDB, an embedded key-value database, in native memory and on the executor's local disk, and uploads its files to the streaming checkpoint for fault tolerance.
- [Runtime filter](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Runtime_filter): A runtime filter is a filter that a query engine builds while a join is running from the join keys of the smaller, filtered input and applies to the larger input before the join, so that rows which cannot find a match are dropped early.
- [Ryan Blue](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Ryan_Blue): Ryan Blue is a software engineer known as one of the original creators of Apache Iceberg, an open table format for large analytic datasets.
- [Salting](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Salting): Salting is a manual technique for data skew in which a random number, the salt, is added to a hot join or grouping key so that the rows for that key are spread over several tasks instead of one.
- [Scala 2.12 and 2.13 in Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Scala_2.12_and_2.13_in_Spark): Scala 2.12 and 2.13 in Spark refers to the two Scala versions that Apache Spark was built for during the Spark 3 series, and to the requirement that Scala and Java applications, libraries and connectors use the same Scala version as the Spark build they run on.
- [Session window](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Session_window): In stream processing, a session window is a window whose length is set by the data: it opens with a record for a key, extends each time another record for that key arrives within a gap duration, and closes when no record arrives for the length of the gap.
- [Shuffle](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Shuffle): A shuffle is the step in a distributed query engine that redistributes data across the cluster so that it is grouped differently across partitions, for example so that all rows with the same key end up in the same task.
- [Shuffle hash join](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Shuffle_hash_join): A shuffle hash join is a distributed equality-join strategy that repartitions both inputs by the join keys, then builds a hash table from one input partition inside each join task.
- [Small files problem](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Small_files_problem): The small files problem is the slowdown and extra cost that occur when a table's data is spread across many files that are much smaller than the size the storage and query engines work best with.
- [Sort-merge join](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Sort-merge_join): A sort-merge join is a distributed equality-join strategy that repartitions both inputs by the join keys, sorts each resulting partition by those keys, and merges the two ordered streams.
- [Spark 3 to Spark 4 migration](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_3_to_Spark_4_migration): Spark 3 to Spark 4 migration is the work of moving Apache Spark applications from the 3.x line (in practice 3.5) to Spark 4.0 or later, the first major release since 3.0.
- [Spark configuration precedence](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_configuration_precedence): In Apache Spark, configuration precedence is the order in which Spark merges property values from the defaults file, the spark-submit command line and application code, and the rule that decides which of those values can still change after the application has started.
- [Spark Connect](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Connect): Spark Connect is a client-server interface for Apache Spark in which a thin client library sends DataFrame operations to a remote Spark server as unresolved logical plans and receives the results over the network.
- [Spark Connect client](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Connect_client): A Spark Connect client is a library that lets an application use Apache Spark remotely through the Spark Connect protocol: it builds unresolved logical plans as Protocol Buffers messages, sends them to a Spark Connect server over gRPC, and decodes the results, which come back as Apache Arrow record batches.
- [Spark Connect plugin](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Connect_plugin): A Spark Connect plugin is a server-side class that extends Spark Connect in Apache Spark with new relations, expressions or commands: the client packs a custom Protocol Buffers message into an extension field of the Spark Connect protocol, and the plugin on the server turns that message into a Spark logical plan, a Catalyst expression, or an action.
- [Spark Connect server](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Connect_server): The Spark Connect server is the server side of Spark Connect in Apache Spark: a gRPC service that runs inside a Spark driver, accepts unresolved logical plans from remote clients, runs them in per-client Spark sessions and streams the results back as Apache Arrow batches.
- [Spark Declarative Pipelines](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Declarative_Pipelines): Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) is a framework in Apache Spark for building batch and streaming data pipelines by declaring the datasets a pipeline should produce and the queries that fill them, while Spark handles execution order, parallelism, checkpoints and retries.
- [Spark error classes](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_error_classes): In Apache Spark, error classes (now documented as error conditions) are the structured identifiers that Spark attaches to user-facing errors: a stable name such as DIVIDE_BY_ZERO, an optional sub-condition, a five-character SQLSTATE code and a message template with named parameters.
- [Spark event log](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_event_log): The Spark event log is a file, or a directory of files, in which an Apache Spark application records the listener events that its driver posts for jobs, stages, tasks, executors and SQL query executions, so that the application's Spark UI can be rebuilt after it ends.
- [Spark History Server](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_History_Server): The Spark History Server is a long-running Apache Spark service that reads the event logs of applications and rebuilds their Spark UI, so that jobs, stages, SQL queries and executors can be inspected after an application has finished.
- [Spark Kubernetes pod template](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Kubernetes_pod_template): In Apache Spark, a Kubernetes pod template is a YAML or JSON pod specification that Spark uses as the starting point when it builds the driver pod or the executor pods of an application on Kubernetes.
- [Spark Kubernetes shuffle storage](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Kubernetes_shuffle_storage): In Apache Spark, shuffle storage on Kubernetes is the set of pod volumes where executors write shuffle files and spill data; by default these are Kubernetes emptyDir volumes that last only as long as the executor pod.
- [Spark listener](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_listener): A Spark listener is a class that Apache Spark calls back when something happens inside an application, such as a job starting, a task ending, an executor being added or a SQL query finishing.
- [Spark memory management](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_memory_management): Spark memory management is the way Apache Spark divides the memory of each executor between running tasks, cached data, user code and the JVM itself.
- [Spark on Kubernetes](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_on_Kubernetes): Spark on Kubernetes is the mode of Apache Spark in which Kubernetes is the cluster manager: the Spark driver and each executor run as Kubernetes pods, and Spark asks the Kubernetes API server for executor pods directly through its native Kubernetes scheduler backend.
- [Spark on YARN](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_on_YARN): Spark on YARN is the deployment of Apache Spark applications on Apache Hadoop YARN (Yet Another Resource Negotiator), where the YARN ResourceManager grants containers on cluster nodes and Spark runs its application master, its driver (in cluster mode) and its executors inside those containers.
- [Spark plugin](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_plugin): A Spark plugin is a class implementing org.apache.spark.api.plugin.SparkPlugin that Apache Spark loads into an application at startup, running one component inside the driver and one inside every executor.
- [Spark resource profiles](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_resource_profiles): In Apache Spark, a resource profile (ResourceProfile) is a set of executor and task resource requirements, such as cores, memory and GPUs, that Spark applies to one stage of a job instead of to the whole application.
- [Spark SQL ANSI mode](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_SQL_ANSI_mode): In Apache Spark, ANSI mode is the Spark SQL dialect, controlled by spark.sql.ansi.enabled, in which invalid operations such as integer overflow, division by zero and malformed casts raise runtime errors instead of returning null or a wrapped value, and type coercion follows rules aligned with the ANSI SQL standard.
- [Spark SQL scripting](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_SQL_scripting): In Apache Spark, SQL scripting is the procedural extension of Spark SQL that runs a block of statements written between BEGIN and END, with local variables, loops, conditional logic and error handlers, as a single request.
- [Spark standalone cluster manager](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_standalone_cluster_manager): The Spark standalone cluster manager is the cluster manager that ships with Apache Spark: a master process and one worker process per node, started with scripts in Spark's sbin directory, that allocate executors to Spark applications without an external resource manager such as YARN or Kubernetes.
- [Spark Streaming (DStreams)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Streaming_(DStreams)): Spark Streaming, also called the DStream API, is the original stream processing library of Apache Spark, in which a live data stream is divided into small batches and represented as a discretized stream (DStream): a continuous series of RDDs, each holding the data received in one time interval.
- [Spark Thrift Server](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_Thrift_Server): The Spark Thrift Server is the JDBC/ODBC server of Apache Spark SQL: a long-running Spark application that implements the HiveServer2 Thrift protocol, so that BI tools, SQL clients and the beeline shell can run SQL on Spark over standard JDBC or ODBC connections without writing Spark code.
- [Spark UI](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark_UI): The Spark UI is the web interface that the driver of an Apache Spark application serves while the application runs, by default at http://:4040, to show the application's jobs, stages, tasks, cached data, configuration, executors and SQL queries.
- [spark-submit](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark-submit): spark-submit is the command-line script in the bin directory of Apache Spark that launches a packaged Spark application (a JAR, a Python file or an R file) on a local machine or on any supported cluster manager through one interface.
- [spark.mllib (RDD-based API)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spark.mllib_(RDD-based_API)): spark.mllib is the original, RDD-based API of MLlib, the machine learning library of Apache Spark, found in the org.apache.spark.mllib package in Scala and Java and pyspark.mllib in Python.
- [SparkContext](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/SparkContext): In Apache Spark, a SparkContext is the object in the driver) that represents the connection to a Spark cluster; it acquires executors, schedules work on them and is used to create RDDs, accumulators and broadcast variables.
- [SparkR](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/SparkR): SparkR is the R package that ships with Apache Spark and lets R programs use Spark: it provides a distributed data frame, the SparkDataFrame, with selection, filtering and aggregation, and access to Spark's machine learning library.
- [SparkSession](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/SparkSession): In Apache Spark, a SparkSession is the entry point for programming with the DataFrame and Dataset API: it reads data, runs SQL, holds session configuration and temporary views, and gives access to the catalog.
- [Speculative execution](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Speculative_execution): In Apache Spark, speculative execution is a scheduler feature that launches a second copy of a task that is running much slower than the other tasks in its stage, on another executor, and uses whichever copy finishes first.
- [Spill (memory)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Spill_(memory)): Spill is the act of a query engine writing intermediate data from memory to local disk while an operation runs, because the data for a sort, aggregation, join or shuffle does not fit in the memory the operation is allowed to use.
- [SQL pipe syntax](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/SQL_pipe_syntax): SQL pipe syntax is an extension of SQL in which a query is written as a sequence of operators joined by the pipe symbol |>, each operator taking the table produced by the previous one, so that the query reads top to bottom in the order of its logical transformations.
- [State store](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/State_store): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, a state store is the versioned key-value store in which stateful operators keep the data they carry from one micro-batch to the next, such as running aggregates, deduplication keys, buffered join rows and user state.
- [Stateful stream processing](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Stateful_stream_processing): Stateful stream processing is stream processing in which the result for a record depends on information kept from earlier records, such as a running count, the last value seen for a key, or rows waiting for a join partner.
- [Stream processing](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Stream_processing): Stream processing is the continuous computation of results over data that has no defined end, in which an engine processes records as they arrive and keeps its output up to date instead of waiting for a complete dataset.
- [Stream-static join](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Stream-static_join): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, a stream-static join joins a streaming DataFrame with a static DataFrame, for example a stream of orders with a table of customers.
- [Stream-stream join](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Stream-stream_join): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, a stream-stream join joins two streaming DataFrames, so that each new row from one stream is matched with rows that have arrived, or will arrive, on the other.
- [Streaming checkpoint](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Streaming_checkpoint): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, a streaming checkpoint is the directory, set with the checkpointLocation option, where a streaming query records which input offsets each micro-batch covered, which batches finished, and the state of its stateful operators, so that after a failure or a restart the query continues exactly where it stopped.
- [Streaming deduplication](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Streaming_deduplication): In Apache Spark Structured Streaming, streaming deduplication is removing repeated records from a stream by a unique identifier, so that each event is passed on once even if the source delivers it several times.
- [Streaming lakehouse](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Streaming_lakehouse): A streaming lakehouse is a data architecture in which streaming jobs write directly into tables in an open table format, so that the same tables serve both streaming readers, which consume new changes incrementally, and batch readers, which query a consistent snapshot.
- [Structured Streaming](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Structured_Streaming): Structured Streaming is the stream processing engine of Apache Spark, built on the Spark SQL engine, in which a streaming computation is written with the same DataFrame and Dataset operations as a batch computation on static data.
- [Time travel (SQL)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Time_travel_(SQL)): Time travel in SQL is a query that reads a table as it was at an earlier version or point in time, written in Apache Spark SQL as SELECT ...
- [transformWithState](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/TransformWithState): In Structured Streaming, transformWithState is the operator for arbitrary stateful processing: user code, written as a stateful processor class, receives the rows for each grouping key, keeps any number of typed state variables for that key across micro-batches, registers timers and emits zero or more output rows.
- [Trigger (Structured Streaming)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Trigger_(Structured_Streaming)): In Structured Streaming, a trigger is the setting on a streaming query that decides when the query processes data and which execution mode runs it: micro-batches as fast as possible, micro-batches on a fixed interval, all available data and then stop, or one of the low-latency modes.
- [Trino](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Trino): Trino is an open source distributed SQL query engine for analytical queries over large datasets.
- [Unity Catalog](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Unity_Catalog): Unity Catalog is an open source data catalog for tables, files, functions and machine learning models in an open lakehouse.
- [User-defined function (Spark)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/User-defined_function_(Spark)): In Apache Spark, a user-defined function (UDF) is a function written by the user in Scala, Java, Python or SQL and registered with Spark so that it can be called on columns of a DataFrame or in a Spark SQL query, like a built-in function.
- [Variant type](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Variant_type): A variant (SQL type VARIANT) is a data type for semi-structured data such as JSON, in which each value carries its own structure in a compact binary encoding, so that rows in the same column can have different shapes and nested fields can be read by path without a fixed schema.
- [Velox](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Velox): Velox is an open source C++ library that provides the execution layer of a data processing engine: columnar vectors, vectorized expression evaluation, functions and relational operators, which other systems embed instead of writing their own.
- [Watermark](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Watermark): In stream processing, a watermark is a moving timestamp that tells the engine how far event time has progressed in a stream, so that it can treat earlier event times as complete, emit final results for them and discard the state it kept for them.
- [Whole-stage code generation](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Whole-stage_code_generation): Whole-stage code generation is the technique by which Apache Spark compiles a chain of physical operators, such as a scan, a filter, a projection and a partial aggregation, into a single generated Java function at run time.
- [Window functions](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Window_functions): A window function is a SQL function that computes a value for each row from a group of related rows, called the window, without collapsing those rows into one as GROUP BY does; in Apache Spark it is written as a function followed by an OVER clause that names the partitioning, the ordering and an optional frame.
- [Windowing (stream processing)](https://openlakehouse.io/wiki/Windowing_(stream_processing)): In stream processing, windowing is dividing an unbounded stream into finite groups of records, usually by time, so that aggregations such as counts and averages can be computed and emitted for each group.

## Data Engineering Reference Architectures
- [Data Engineering Reference Architectures](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures): Open source data engineering reference architectures: interactive, runnable blueprints for batch and streaming medallion pipelines, real-time streaming, multi-engine catalogs, governed AI agents and data sharing, mapped to industry use cases and backed by public repositories.
- [Machine-readable catalog (JSON)](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures.json): Every architecture, component and industry lens as JSON.
- [The agentic lakehouse: Omnigent and MLflow over sandboxed Spark Connect sessions, on Iceberg and Unity Catalog](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/agentic-lakehouse): Agents get a sandbox, a Spark session and a catalog identity. The platform decides the rest. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/agentic-lakehouse.md
- [Batch medallion with Spark Declarative Pipelines: Spark 4.3, Apache Iceberg and Unity Catalog with bronze, silver and gold](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/batch-medallion): Declare the tables, let Spark work out the order, keep every layer in an open format. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/batch-medallion.md
- [Change data capture with SCD type 2: AUTO CDC in Spark Declarative Pipelines, from a Kafka change feed into Apache Iceberg](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/change-data-capture): Keep the current state and every past version of each row, without hand-written MERGE logic. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/change-data-capture.md
- [Streaming medallion: Kafka, Spark Structured Streaming and Apache Iceberg in Unity Catalog](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/streaming-medallion): Events in, governed tables out, seconds behind the source. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/streaming-medallion.md
- [Real-time streaming with Spark Real-Time Mode: Kafka in, Kafka out, milliseconds in between](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/real-time-streaming): Continuous processing for fraud, recommendations and live boards, measured end to end. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/real-time-streaming.md
- [One catalog, many engines: Unity Catalog OSS with Spark, DuckDB, PyIceberg and Trino on Delta and Iceberg](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/multi-engine-catalog): Write once, read from whatever engine fits the question. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/multi-engine-catalog.md
- [Governed AI agents for data engineering: Spark Declarative Pipelines, Spark Connect, Kubernetes and a governed Iceberg REST catalog](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/governed-ai-agents): Agents write pipeline specs; the platform decides what they are allowed to touch. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/governed-ai-agents.md
- [Open data sharing: Delta Sharing servers over Unity Catalog and open tables](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/open-data-sharing): Share live tables with another organization without copying them or sending files. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/open-data-sharing.md
- [The open lakehouse on a laptop: Spark 4.3, Apache Iceberg, Unity Catalog, Kafka, Airflow, MLflow and an agent, in Docker](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/laptop-open-lakehouse): The whole stack, one service at a time, on the machine in front of you. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/laptop-open-lakehouse.md
- [Policy pushdown and open lineage: Cedar policies compiled to CEL, enforced in Spark and DataFusion, with OpenLineage](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/policy-and-lineage): Write access rules once, enforce them inside every engine, and record where every column came from. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/policy-and-lineage.md
- [Semantic layer with Spark metric views: Metrics declared in YAML, served over Spark Connect to BI, notebooks and agents](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/semantic-layer): Define revenue once. Every dashboard, notebook and agent gets the same number. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/semantic-layer.md
- [ML and GenAI lifecycle on the lakehouse: MLflow tracking, registry and AI Gateway over open tables](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/ml-lifecycle): Every model run points at the exact table version it was trained on. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/ml-lifecycle.md
- [Arrow-native serving: Arrow Flight SQL and Spark Connect clients over lakehouse tables](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/arrow-native-serving): Results leave as Arrow columns, not rows, in whatever language the client speaks. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/arrow-native-serving.md
- [Self-hosted catalog on AWS: Unity Catalog OSS on ECS Fargate with Neon Postgres and S3, in Terraform](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/cloud-deployment-aws): The open catalog in your own AWS account, with no static storage keys. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/cloud-deployment-aws.md
- [Serverless lakehouse services: Catalog and lineage as Neon Functions on branchable Postgres](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/serverless-lakehouse-services): Every pull request gets its own catalog, database and bucket. Markdown: https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/serverless-lakehouse-services.md

## Open source data engineering resources
- [open-lakehouse (Runnable stacks and courses)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/open-lakehouse): Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Kafka, Airflow and MLflow in Docker, with an AWS path.
- [unitycatalog-playground (Runnable stacks and courses)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/unitycatalog-playground): Unity Catalog OSS with Spark, Delta and Iceberg in marimo notebooks.
- [lakehouse-masterclass (Runnable stacks and courses)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/lakehouse-masterclass): A textbook course that builds an open lakehouse one service per chapter.
- [Spark Masterclass (Runnable stacks and courses)](https://open-lakehouse.github.io/spark-masterclass/): A runnable online book on Apache Spark 4.3; every number traces to a script.
- [spark-demos (Runnable stacks and courses)](https://github.com/lisancao/spark-demos): One runnable demo per Spark feature: metric views, Spark Connect, Real-Time Mode and more.
- [safe-spark-agents-paper (Runnable stacks and courses)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/safe-spark-agents-paper): A reproducible study and reference architecture for AI agents building Spark pipelines.
- [Delta Lake (Open table formats)](https://github.com/delta-io/delta): Transaction-log table format; the protocol is in PROTOCOL.md.
- [delta-rs (Open table formats)](https://github.com/delta-io/delta-rs): Native Rust and Python library for Delta tables, no JVM.
- [delta-kernel-rs (Open table formats)](https://github.com/delta-io/delta-kernel-rs): A Rust kernel that engines embed to read and write Delta.
- [Apache Iceberg (Open table formats)](https://github.com/apache/iceberg): Metadata-tree table format with a REST catalog specification.
- [PyIceberg (Open table formats)](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python): Pure-Python Iceberg reads and writes.
- [iceberg-rust (Open table formats)](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-rust): The Rust implementation of Apache Iceberg.
- [Apache Hudi (Open table formats)](https://github.com/apache/hudi): Table format built around upserts and incremental queries.
- [Unity Catalog OSS (Catalogs)](https://github.com/unitycatalog/unitycatalog): Tables, volumes, functions and models, with Iceberg REST and credential vending.
- [Apache Polaris (Catalogs)](https://github.com/apache/polaris): An implementation of the Iceberg REST catalog specification.
- [Lakekeeper (Catalogs)](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper): Iceberg REST catalog in Rust.
- [unitycatalog-rs (Catalogs)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/unitycatalog-rs): Rust implementation of the Unity Catalog OSS APIs.
- [Apache Spark (Compute engines)](https://github.com/apache/spark): Batch, SQL, Structured Streaming and declarative pipelines.
- [Apache Flink (Compute engines)](https://github.com/apache/flink): Stateful stream processing.
- [Trino (Compute engines)](https://github.com/trinodb/trino): Distributed SQL across catalogs.
- [DuckDB (Compute engines)](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb): In-process analytical SQL.
- [Apache DataFusion (Compute engines)](https://github.com/apache/datafusion): Embeddable Rust query engine on Arrow.
- [Polars (Compute engines)](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars): Arrow-native DataFrames in Rust and Python.
- [Apache Kafka (Streaming and ingestion)](https://github.com/apache/kafka): The event log most streaming architectures start from.
- [Debezium (Streaming and ingestion)](https://github.com/debezium/debezium): Change data capture from database logs.
- [spark-rtm-quickstart (Streaming and ingestion)](https://github.com/lisancao/spark-rtm-quickstart): Spark Real-Time Mode pipelines with a latency harness.
- [Apache Airflow (Orchestration)](https://github.com/apache/airflow): Python DAG scheduler.
- [Dagster (Orchestration)](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster): Asset-oriented orchestration.
- [Temporal (Orchestration)](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal): Durable execution for long-running workflows.
- [OpenLineage (Governance, lineage and policy)](https://github.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage): Open standard for lineage events.
- [Marquez (Governance, lineage and policy)](https://github.com/MarquezProject/marquez): Reference OpenLineage server and UI.
- [policast (Governance, lineage and policy)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/policast): Cedar policies compiled to CEL and enforced inside Spark and DataFusion plans.
- [breakwater (Governance, lineage and policy)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/breakwater): Cedar row filters and column masks for DataFusion.
- [open-lineage-connect (Governance, lineage and policy)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/open-lineage-connect): OpenLineage events stored as Delta and Iceberg tables.
- [MLflow (ML and AI)](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow): Tracking, registry, GenAI tracing, evaluation and AI Gateway.
- [lakehouse-agent-kit (ML and AI)](https://github.com/open-lakehouse/lakehouse-agent-kit): Agent skills for the open lakehouse stack.
- [Model Context Protocol (ML and AI)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io): Open protocol for giving agents tools and data.
- [Delta Lake protocol (Specs and protocols)](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/blob/master/PROTOCOL.md): How the Delta transaction log works.
- [Iceberg table spec (Specs and protocols)](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/): Iceberg metadata, manifests and snapshots.
- [Iceberg REST catalog spec (Specs and protocols)](https://iceberg.apache.org/rest-catalog-spec/): The HTTP API catalogs implement for Iceberg.
- [Delta Sharing protocol (Specs and protocols)](https://github.com/delta-io/delta-sharing/blob/main/PROTOCOL.md): REST protocol for sharing live tables.
- [Spark Connect (Specs and protocols)](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/spark-connect-overview.html): Spark's client-server protocol.
- [Arrow Flight SQL (Specs and protocols)](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/FlightSql.html): SQL over Arrow Flight.
- [OpenLineage spec (Specs and protocols)](https://github.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/tree/main/spec): The lineage event model and facets.

## Data engineering architectures by industry
- [Open source data architecture for Banking](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/banking): Banks move core banking ledgers, card authorizations and payment messages into open tables so fraud, risk and regulatory reporting read one governed copy instead of a mart per team.
- [Open source data architecture for Payments and fintech](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/payments-fintech): Payment processors and fintechs run on event streams; the lakehouse holds the durable history that fraud models, reconciliation and merchant analytics read.
- [Open source data architecture for Healthcare providers](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/healthcare): Health systems pull EHR, claims and device data into open tables mapped to a common data model, with strict access policy on every column that identifies a patient.
- [Open source data architecture for Manufacturing](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/manufacturing): Plants stream machine telemetry from the shop floor, join it with MES and ERP records, and use the result for predictive maintenance, quality and OEE.
- [Open source data architecture for Energy and utilities](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/energy-utilities): Utilities combine smart meter interval data, grid telemetry and asset records for load forecasting, outage response and regulatory filings.
- [Open source data architecture for Retail and e-commerce](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/retail-ecommerce): Retailers and online stores bring point-of-sale, clickstream, inventory, supply chain and loyalty data together for demand forecasting, replenishment, personalization and fraud.
- [Open source data architecture for Telecommunications](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/telecommunications): Operators collect network performance counters, call detail records and customer data for network planning, churn and service assurance.
- [Open source data architecture for Cybersecurity](https://openlakehouse.io/reference-architectures/industries/cybersecurity): Security teams keep years of logs in open tables at object-storage prices and run detections, hunts and investigations over them with several engines.

## Blog posts
- [Apache Spark Metric Views: One Definition for Every Dashboard, Application, and AI Agent](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/metric-views-spark-42): Spark 4.2 made it a whole lot easier to define metrics once and query them consistently across an organization, including from dashboards, agents, and applications. They are already dead easy to use; in this blog I review metric views in Spark end to end for SQL lovers.
- [The Top 10 Data Engines in 2026, and What Each One Is Actually For](https://openlakehouse.io/blog/apache-spark/top-10-data-engines-2026): A ranked guide to the ten data engines that matter in 2026 (Apache Spark, Flink, DuckDB, Trino, DataFusion, Polars, ClickHouse, StarRocks, Ray and Velox), what each is best at, where it falls short, and how to choose.
- [Introducing Real-time Mode's Stateful Queries on Spark](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/real-time-mode-spark-43): A walkthrough of Structured Streaming and the stateful queries Spark 4.3 adds to Real-time Mode, using a bookshop that re-ranks its recommendations on every click and measures latency in both micro-batch and Real-time execution.
- [Unity Catalog Volumes: Unstructured Data for the Agentic Lakehouse](https://www.unitycatalog.io/blogs/uc-volumes/): Volumes govern unstructured data in Unity Catalog. Open one in a marimo
- [The Ultimate Guide to Apache Spark 4.3](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/ultimate-guide-spark-43): Everything new in Apache Spark 4.3 and full feature breakdowns for stateful Real-time Mode, SCD Type 2 in Auto CDC, Project Feather, Spark Connect operation IDs and REST endpoints, DataFrame.zip and Python UDF transpilation, ASOF JOIN, JSON_TABLE, VARIANT edits, nanosecond timestamps and more.
- [Spark Connect from Rust: Pull Spark outputs into DuckDB and Polars](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/spark-connect-rust-duckdb-polars): A guide to using the Apache Spark Connect client for Rust to integrate spark with DuckDB and Polars: start a Spark 4.2 server, get a result out as Arrow, hand it to DuckDB 2.0 for an ASOF join and to Polars for a rolling window, and write the answer back to Spark.
- [Apache Iceberg v4 Column Updates Are About to Change Feature Engineering](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/iceberg-column-updates): Iceberg v4 is adding column files, companion files that can hold one or more whole columns for every row of a data file and be swapped in by position at read time. This post explains why that matters for feature stores and other wide tables, where the design helps, and why the v4 work is still not something you can run in production.
- [Building a Spark Connect Client in OCaml](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/build-a-spark-connect-client): How to build a Spark Connect client from the protocol up, in OCaml: compile the spark/connect protos, speak gRPC over HTTP/2 (ExecutePlan, AnalyzePlan, grpc-status-details-bin), build Relation and Expression plan trees with plan_id, decode the Arrow IPC batches each response carries, write Arrow for LocalRelation, and surface Spark error classes and SQLSTATEs. Includes the ocaml-protoc encoding bug behind 'Invalid protobuf byte sequence', a protocol coverage table tested on Spark 4.1.3, 4.2.0 and 4.3.0-rc1, and what the client still can't do.
- [All About Iceberg's File Format API: simplifying the engine/format interface and Parquet's multimodal future](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/iceberg-file-format-api): Apache Iceberg's File Format API (1.11, 1.12) explained with a runnable Java program: FormatModelRegistry keyed on the closed FileFormat enum (Parquet, Avro, ORC) and an open set of engine row types (Spark InternalRow, Flink RowData, Record), ReadBuilder and dataWriteBuilder, the 'Format model is not registered' error, the compatibility kit (TCK), the Vortex PR, and why multimodal support is arriving as Parquet FILE and VECTOR types rather than new file formats.
- [An Idiot's Guide to Spark Connect Clients](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/idiots-guide-spark-connect-clients): Everything you need to go from \"what is Spark?\" to running jobs on a Spark Connect server from Python, Scala, Go, Rust or Swift, and working out what went wrong when it doesn't work.
- [A Field Guide to Apache Iceberg 1.12](https://datacircus.substack.com/p/a-field-guide-to-apache-iceberg-112): This release is a consolidation effort that focuses on correctness, stability, and paving the path for V4 readiness.
- [TUTORIAL: How to Build an Open Lakehouse on Your Laptop](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/open-lakehouse-on-your-laptop): A self-contained tutorial that builds a complete open lakehouse in an empty folder, one layer at a time, from S3-compatible storage and Delta tables through Unity Catalog, Iceberg readers, declarative pipelines, Real-Time Mode and stateful streaming, Airflow and MLflow.
- [Hosting an Entire Open Lakehouse on Port 8080](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/lakehouse-at-home-demos): Building lakehouse-at-home, a desktop stack for testing new Apache Spark and Iceberg releases before demoing them: Spark 4.0 and 4.1 side by side in Docker, Iceberg JDBC catalog on Postgres, SeaweedFS S3, Unity Catalog OSS, Kafka, Airflow with SparkPipelinesOperator, Spark Connect, Real-Time Mode latency on 4.1, and building an Iceberg runtime for a Spark 5.0 snapshot to test AUTO CDC. The exact Hadoop and AWS SDK pins, and every port collision on 8080.
- [Most PySpark Tuning Advice Starts in the Wrong Place](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/python-performance-in-spark): PySpark runs DataFrame code in the JVM at native speed, and almost everything that makes it slow happens where data crosses into Python. Ordered by how much each one bought in my own measurements: stay in the JVM, batch the crossing, don't produce the data, skip pandas for grouped work, take the JVM out of the client, and give Python the memory it actually uses.
- [Stop Blaming Serialization for Slow Python UDFs](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/pyspark-udf-showdown): Spark uses the word Arrow for a pandas conversion setting, a UDF transport and operator, and a data type your function receives. The difference between them is most of the difference in UDF performance, and my own benchmark confused two of them.
- [AUTO_CDC: Turning an event log into current state with Spark Declarative Pipelines](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/auto-cdc-declarative-pipelines): AUTO CDC (create_auto_cdc_flow) in Apache Spark 4.2 Declarative Pipelines, tested on messy data: SCD Type 1, keys, sequence_by, apply_as_deletes, out-of-order and stale events, and which targets work (Iceberg with JDBC, Hive, REST and Glue catalogs) and which don't (Parquet: AUTOCDC_TARGET_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_MERGE; Delta, which lacks SupportsRowLevelOperations). The contract it leaves on your side: a unique, non-null sequence and deletes as events.
- [From Pickle to Arrow: A Decade of Moving Data Between Spark's JVM and Python](https://systemsnull.net/posts/data-engineering-ai/arrow-and-spark): How Apache Arrow replaced pickle at every JVM-to-Python boundary in PySpark, from toPandas() in Spark 2.3 to pandas UDFs, mapInArrow, applyInArrow, Spark Connect, Arrow-optimized Python UDFs (useArrow=True) and @arrow_udf in 4.1, to the 4.2 defaults. Why spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled and spark.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled control different things, with benchmark numbers, and the one conversion that remains inside Spark's own engine.
- [Apache Iceberg 1.11.0 Release](https://iceberg.apache.org/blog/apache-iceberg-1.11.0-release/): Iceberg 1.11.0 lands the biggest REST catalog upgrade since the protocol was introduced, plus encryption, geospatial types, SQL UDFs, Spark 4.1 and Flink 2.1 support, and the first foundations of Format V4.
- [Integrating the Rust Delta Kernel into ClickHouse](https://openlakehouse.io/blog/delta-lake/clickhouse-delta-kernel): How the ClickHouse team adopted delta-kernel-rs to offload Delta protocol handling, unlock writes, schema evolution, time travel, CDF, and pruning — and what it took to ship a Rust library inside a C++ database.
- [Delta Grows Up: Writes, Unity Catalog and Time Travel](https://openlakehouse.io/blog/delta-lake/duckdb-delta-grows-up): DuckDB's Delta and Unity Catalog extensions shed their experimental tags — now with INSERT writes, time travel, Unity Catalog coordination, and Catalog Managed Tables.
- [From Black Box to Observability: Tracing OpenClaw with MLflow](https://openlakehouse.io/blog/agentic/openclaw-tracing): How to add MLflow Tracing to OpenClaw so every autonomous agent run becomes a fully inspectable execution timeline — locally, with your data on your machine.
- [Delta 4.2.0 Released](https://openlakehouse.io/blog/delta-lake/delta-4-2-released): Delta Lake 4.2 advances on two fronts — Kernel expands outward with a new Flink connector, streaming improvements, and broader data type support, while catalog-managed tables mature with atomic operations, schema evolution from SQL, and synchronous UniForm.
- [Delta Lake 4.1.0 Released](https://openlakehouse.io/blog/delta-lake/delta-lake-4-1-0-released): Delta Lake 4.1.0 ships Apache Spark 4.1.0 support, catalog-managed table enhancements, server-side planning, atomic CTAS for UC tables, and conflict-free feature enablement.
- [The Next Evolution of Delta: Catalog-Managed Tables](https://openlakehouse.io/blog/delta-lake/delta-catalog-managed-tables): How catalog-managed commits shift transaction coordination from the filesystem to Unity Catalog, making the catalog the single source of truth for Delta table state.

## Learn
- [Installing Omnigent](https://openlakehouse.io/learn/getting-started/omnigent-install): Install the Omnigent CLI, set up credentials, and launch your first agent in a few minutes.
- [Getting started with Omnigent](https://openlakehouse.io/learn/getting-started/omnigent): Run a coding agent locally with a web UI, inline comments, file editing, and policy enforcement.
- [Getting started with Unity Catalog](https://openlakehouse.io/learn/getting-started/unity-catalog): Five minutes from zero to a working Unity Catalog mental model — the open catalog for data and AI.
- [Getting started with MLflow](https://openlakehouse.io/learn/getting-started/mlflow): Track experiments, package models, and ship ML and GenAI with the open standard.
- [Getting started with Delta Lake](https://openlakehouse.io/learn/getting-started/delta-lake): ACID tables on object storage in five minutes — the open foundation of modern lakehouses.
- [Getting started with Apache Spark](https://openlakehouse.io/learn/getting-started/apache-spark): A quick introduction to using Spark via the interactive shell and self-contained applications.

## Citation policy
All content on this site is republished or original technical material about
open-source projects. When citing a specific post, use the canonical URL
listed above; republished posts may point to their upstream source. When
citing the underlying project, prefer the project's own site.
